19011:
There are two foreign areas around you. One side is the area under the control of the USSR (Soviet Republic) and the second area is that of the Western countries representing the democratic world. So, as there are two foreign countries where you can buy and sell resources, you may need to work with both currencies. 

If you move the camera to one of the edges of the map, you will see the border (Soviet or Western), with its respective customs houses placed alongside. Depending on where you purchase resources, you will spend rubles (Soviet area) or dollars (West area)
19012: Why do I need money in a socialist society?
19013:
In a couple of words: You don't.
In another: Trade.

In your republic, rubles and dollars are only used for foreign exchange. Your internal economy works without any currencies, only with resources.

To reiterate the key point— the two currencies are only present due to trade with foreign countries (Soviet or West). They can be used to obtain resources, especially those you might need now but can't produce yet.

But you choose! You can focus solely on trade, getting money by exporting natural resources or refining imported ones... or you can build up a totally self-sufficient republic and ignore both currencies altogether.
19014: How do I actually get rubles or dollars?
19015:
You can load resources onto a truck or a train wagon and deliver them to a customs house. If you bring resources to the Soviet border you will get rubles. If you will bring resources to the West border you will get dollars.

If you click on the customs house building, you can see the prices you'll receive if you deliver goods there.

19020: How can I get citizens to move into residential buildings?
19021:
After you construct a residential building, you have two options to get citizens to move in:

Option 1: Invite immigrants for money
You can invest some of your rubles or dollars to invite immigrants to your building. Click on the building where you would like new citizens. Then click on [IMG editor/worker_buyrub.png] "Invite from Soviet countries" (spends ruble) or [IMG editor/worker_buyusd.png] "Invite from third world" (spends dollars). Immigrants from third-world countries can be hungrier, in poor health, and/or uneducated, but they are cheaper to invite.

Option 2: Move from another building
You can relocate citizens from one residential building to another. Click on the source building that you want to move citizens from. Click on [IMG editor/tool_worker_relocate.png] "Relocate citizens," Then just click on the building you would like the citizens to move to.
19022: How do I get citizens to go to work?
19023:
If you have citizens living in your residential buildings, you can send them to work. You have two options:

Option 1: A factory/workplace close to their home.
If there is a factory or any other workplace where the workers are needed close to their residential building, workers will go to it on foot. You can check if any building is reachable for workers/citizens on foot by mousing over [IMG editor/btab_walking.png] icon in the building's window.

Option 2: Transport workers to a workplace.
If no workplace can be reached by foot, you can transport citizens to their workplace by bus or train.
Build the "Train platform" [IMG editor/tool_rail_station_passanger.png] or the "Bus platform" [IMG editor/tool_road_busstation.png] near residential buildings. You will see workers waiting on those platforms. Define this platform as the first stop in the vehicle's schedule, then define the destination (factory, workplace) as a second station. Later, you can build a platform near your factories or workplaces. Workers will step off a bus or train and walk to the various workplaces without having to be dropped off at each specific one.
19024: How can I tweak a building's productivity?
19025:
Sometimes you want a factory or other building to work only at a fraction of its capacity.

For example, you may have a food factory, but you do not have enough crops to produce food. The result is that many workers are keeping the factory running at 100%% capacity, but there are only enough crops to run the factory at 20%% capacity. The other 80%% aren't actually contributing labor to your republic!

You can use the productivity tweak buttons:

•[IMA editor/btab_productivity_increase.png]Increase productivity

•[IMA editor/btab_productivity_decrease.png]Decrease productivity

This way, you can simply select how many workers should go there and at what level the factory or building should be running at. You can decrease the productivity when you don't need it at 100%%, and if more production is needed you can increase its productivity.

You can do this for all buildings where there are workers (mines, factories, shops, etc.).
19026: How do I purchase resources I don't have?
19027:
In any building where resources can be stored or spent, you can purchase resources for money (rubles or dollars).

For example, if you built a food factory and you would like to produce food, but you're missing the crops, you can click on the "Purchase resources" icons [IMG editor/buy_rub.png] [IMG editor/buy_dollar.png] and pay for crops (or whatever you need).

After you open the window where you can purchase the resources, you will see two tabs:

•Automatic purchase - here you can set a required amount of the resource. If the resource decreases below this limit, the resource will be automatically purchased again to equal the required amount.

•Manual purchase - this is a one-time purchase of the resource. After resources are used, no automatic additional purchases will be made.

A suggested best practice for any factories or shops is to set an automatic purchase of resources of about 20%%-50%% of the storage capacity. This ensures the factory will not stop production due to lack of resources, whilst leaving space for any resources you manufacture yourself to be stored as well.
19029:
Global market prices shift every couple of days.

The prices change because of:

•Random market fluctuation

•Inflation

•Demand on the market increasing via your resource imports (purchases), driving the price up

•Supply on the market increasing via your resource exports, driving the price down

•Some global events, which drastically increase or decrease prices of resources for limited time

•New technology that affects the amount of manpower or resources needed to manufacture goods, resulting in a global market shift 

Note: If there is a change in the price of coal, it also changes prices on all products which are manufactured from coal, as well as the prices of all buildings and vehicles. 

All prices are ultimately defined by price of their input resources, so all prices in the game are dynamic.

19061:
Factories are buildings where resources are transformed into a different product.

For example, the steel mill needs coal [IMG resources/coal.png] and iron [IMG resources/iron.png] to manufacture steel [IMG resources/steel.png].

Naturally, besides the resources, you also need manpower: workers to toil in the factories. 

If workers or resources are not at the factory, the factory will cease production. Also, if the output storage(s) are full of manufactured products, the factory will halt production.

You can extend factory input or output storages by connecting the factory to additional storage or warehouses. See additional topics to discover more.
19101:
Citizens divide their day into two time periods:

1) Working 

During work time, citizens will try to get to a workplace (children try to get to a school). First, they check to see if there are any free jobs near their home. If not, they then go to a transit platform where they wait for any available transport to commute to a location where they can work.

You can recognize citizens trying to commute to work by this symbol [IMG editor/workers_workers.png]

2) Free time 

After the citizens finish work, they try to fulfill their needs and demands, such as getting to a shop for some groceries, or doing an activity according to their preferences.

You can recognize the citizens trying to enjoy their free time by this icon [IMG editor/workers_passangers.png]
19103:
Adult citizens have three education levels. You can tell the difference by the different icons shown in workplace menus.

[IMG editor/workers_workers_noedu.png] No education - these citizens can only go to school. They are not yet qualified for any of the jobs available in your society.

[IMG editor/workers_workers_loedu.png] Basic education - these citizens can do most available jobs, except those that require a university education.

[IMG editor/workers_workers_hiedu.png] University education - these citizens can work on any job, but they will primarily try to engage in those jobs that require their advanced education (like teacher, doctor, researcher, etc.).

You can tell the different age-tiers of children (future workers) by these symbols:

[IMG editor/workers_childs0.png] 0 - 6 years old

[IMG editor/workers_childs2.png] 7-12 years old

[IMG editor/workers_childs1.png] 12 - 16 years old

[IMG editor/workers_childs3.png] 17- 21 years old

Children or adult citizens without an education will spend their work period trying to get to a school to study for their basic education.
19105:
If a citizen finishes their education at a school, they can move on to study at university.

1) If the citizen is 21+ years old, you'll need to use the relocate tool [IMG editor/tool_worker_relocate.png] to them to a university residence hall.

[IMA editor/tool_internat1.png]

This is a special residential building; these citizens will use 100% of their work periods to study instead of looking for a job at a workplace.

At the end of their studies, the citizen will try to move into an available flat nearby. If the citizen cannot find a nearby flat, you can relocate them manually with [IMG editor/tool_worker_relocate.png].

2) If the citizen has finished school during their childhood (under 21 years old), they will spend their work period trying to get into university. They don't need to be placed into a university halls of residence.
19107:
Citizens in transit are divided into three groups:

[IMG editor/workers_workers.png] Workers: Citizens commuting to work 

[IMG editor/workers_passangers.png] Passengers: Citizens enjoying their free time and trying to reach services like shops, cinemas, etc.

[IMG editor/workers_childs.png] Students: Citizens traveling to their place of education.

Citizens will wait on the station/platform. When a bus or train/tram comes to the station/platform, every citizen checks the vehicle's next scheduled stop to see if the bus or train is going to a place they are interested in. If it is, they board. 

E.G. :
If a bus arrives at the station and its next destination is a workplace or a station that's only close to factories, no passengers (citizens on free time) or students will board.

If another bus arrives and its next destination is a station near a university, only the students going to study at the university (and the teachers/staff that work there) will board.

You can decide which citizens are allowed to board at each stop on a vehicle's line. To control this, open the vehicle or line window and choose a stop from the schedule, then check or uncheck the relevant boxes to create boarding rules.

Warning: if a citizen is stuck on transportation for too long, they will leave the vehicle and appear back at their home.
19109:
Simply put, every adult citizen can have a baby. 

If a citizen is too hungry or too sick., they are less likely to be able to have a baby.

Birth rates depend on how good life is for citizens.
19111:
Every citizen has a health level. [IMA editor/status_health.png] 

This level is affected by many factors. 
E.G. If a citizen drinks alcohol, their health is decreased. If a citizen is hungry too long, their health is also decreased.

Every citizen has a lifespan — their expected length of life. Lifespan is affected by many factors like pollution, happiness, and health.

Every citizen can potentially fall ill. Pollution of their living area can affect the chance. Global events, like an epidemic, can also rapidly affect the chances of falling sick.

•If health is less than 50%%, the citizen will demand a hospital visit
•If health is less than 30%%, the citizen will not be able to work due to sickness
•If health is less than 20%%, health will be constantly lost unless an ambulance can save them. 

Citizens will die if:
•Their health level reaches 0%%
•They reach their lifespan age (expected length of life)
19113:
Every citizen has a happiness level [IMA editor/status_happiness.png].

Happiness is affected by many factors, but basically, if a citizen gets what they want, their happiness level goes up; if not, happiness goes down. 

If citizens drink alcohol, their happiness goes up faster than with other activities. However, drinking alcohol can negatively affect health.

If their happiness level reaches 0%%, citizens will flee your republic.
19114: Do my citizens have what they need?
19115:
In general, all demands affect happiness if they are not met [IMG editor/status_happiness.png].

Certain demands are satisfied when citizens visit a store/shop where the goods they require are stored. Shops need workers [IMG editor/workers_workers_loedu.png] (sellers) to keep these shops running. The amount of workers in a shop impacts how many customers [IMG editor/workers_passangers_half.png] can receive goods there.

[IMG resources/food.png] Food: Basic food demand. It affects hunger level (how sated a citizen is). If satiety is too low, health is affected.

[IMG resources/meat.png] Meat: Additional food demand. This also primarily affects satiety. Compared to basic foodstuffs, meat has some advantages, giving citizens higher health and happiness (no vegans in your republic!).

[IMG resources/clothes.png] Clothes: Basic demand for clothes in good repair. If the quality level of citizens' clothing is too low, it will affect the citizen's happiness and health (especially during winter). 

[IMG resources/eletronics.png] Electronics: An additional, optional demand that represents the level of personal consumer electronics your citizen has access to. A level of 1.0 means the citizen owns a radio, 2.0 means they own a TV, and 3.0 means they own a computer.
19117:
Each citizen decides every day what they would like to do (activity).

According to the following levels, activities are chosen randomly during each free period. The higher the level, the higher the base chance is that this activity will be chosen.

[IMG editor/status_sport.png] Local Sports
Satisfied by visiting a sports facility.

[IMG editor/status_religion.png] Spirituality 
Satisfied by visiting a church

[IMG editor/status_alcohol.png] Drinking
Satisfied by visiting a pub.

[IMG editor/status_culture.png] Culture
Satisfied by visiting a theater, cinema, etc.

If a demand is not fulfilled, the happiness level [IMG editor/status_happiness.png] of the citizen is decreased and the citizen's preference for the unfulfilled demand is also reduced.

If a demand is fulfilled, a citizen's happiness level is increased and they will seek out that demand more often.
19119:
[IMA editor/status_religion.png]

If you selected a map where there are churches present, citizens can satisfy their spiritual demand by visiting these churches.

[IMA editor/tool_civ_kirche1.png] [IMA editor/tool_civ_kostolik.png]

However, you are a socialist government, set against any religion, so you cannot build any more churches.

So it is up to you. You can leave the churches open and let the citizens satisfy their religious demands, but if a citizen demands and has access to a church and they do not have many other activities to occupy them, this demand will constantly get higher and higher as they continue attending. Then, even moving them to a location where there is no church will not stop them from demanding a church.

It is recommended to close churches (with [IMG editor/btab_productivity_decrease.png] "decrease productivity" ) before citizens' spirituality demand level is too high, and instead let citizens join in activities you can more easily satisfy.
19120: Are my citizens loyal to the cause?
19121:
Government loyalty represents how much loyalty your citizens feel toward your government.

[IMA editor/status_soviet.png]

If the value is too low, citizens will react more negatively when they miss something. If the value is below 30%%, it can affect also their happiness, which will decrease more as loyalty continues to drop.

If the value is high, citizens will not react as negatively when they miss something. Their productivity will also be higher.

In certain buildings, the loyalty of the workers will affect the citizens they're attending to, whether they're inmates at a prison, radio listeners, or students. In those buildings, you can dictate which citizens are allowed to work there, in order to prevent negative effect on other citizens.

However, you won't known the government loyalty of your citizens unless the secret police agents are surveilling them using spy equipment installed in their homes. If a citizen's loyalty is unknown, they will be allowed to work in these buildings, even if their true loyalty is less than the value you set.

If you want to increase the government loyalty of your citizens, you should first start with building some monuments. However, these have a limited effect, and can only increase loyalty to a maximum of 50%%.

To increase loyalty above this, you need to run propaganda via broadcasts. You can also restrict low-loyalty employees from teaching in school and universities, so students will come out more loyal. You can give a personal cars to citizens — this also increase the loyalty. But don't forget to keep the secret police active, otherwise those restrictions will be not so effective!
19123:
If citizens have a young child (0-6 years), they cannot go to work unless they can place the child in a kindergarten. 

[TOOL CWC_Kindergarten1] 

It is recommended to have a kindergarten in the residential area, to release extra workers (parents). You lose a few workers to the staffing of the kindergarten, but you gain many more workers freed from childcare and able to return to work.
19125:
It is highly recommended to have schools because if you have children, they can learn during their childhood. Then when they reach adult age, they will be able to go to work immediately.

[TOOL CWC_School1]

Teachers working in schools require a university education.

The number of teachers [IMG editor/workers_workers_hiedu.png] and staff [IMG editor/workers_workers_loedu.png] determines the maximum number of students [IMG editor/workers_childs.png]. If the number of students is more than this maximum, the remainder of the students will wait in the schoolyard for classes to become available.
19200: How do I build with my own resources?
19201:
If you want to construct something without using money, first you need to check the checkbox in the right bottom corner of the screen:

[IMG editor/icon_construction.png] [IMG editor/checkbox_on.png] [LANGSTR 67091]

Now when you place a building, instead of automatically being built using money, the new planned construction will be ready for assignment to a construction office.

If you're building infrastructure (road, rails, pipelines, etc.), you will first see a blueprint of the planned construction (displayed as white with a black outline). You can freely add and delete without spending any money or resources.

When you are finished with your design and you would like to start construction of the infrastructure you have planned, click on the "Start construction" button:

[IMG editor/btab_start_construction.png] [LANGSTR 1081]

This will change the blueprint plans into a regular construction which can be assigned to a construction office.
19202: Can I use my own vehicles to terraform?
19203:
If you have unchecked "Auto-build from rubles and dollars" and want to raise, lower, or level terrain, you need to have some excavators (raise, lower) or bulldozers (level).

[IMA editor/tool_terrain_raise.png] [IMA editor/tool_terrain_lower.png] is done by [IMA vehicles/service_caterpilar_big/preview.dds]


[IMA editor/tool_terrain_smooth_editor.png] [IMA editor/tool_terrain_level3.png] is done by [IMA vehicles/service_bulldozer_big/preview.dds]

You need to have these vehicles in a depot or construction office that is somewhat close to the place where you want to do groundworks. The maximum distance is 1000 meters.
19204: How do I use the construction office?
19205:
Construction offices are required to create buildings using your own resources.

Click on [CATEGORY constindustry].

Choose [TOOL construction_office2].

After the construction office is built, open its window. You can then specify sources for resources and purchase vehicles. You are now ready to assign constructions.

Click on the "Specify or replace a source building" [IMG editor/tool_building_addsource.png] and you can assign a source building. Source buildings store resources for construction. For example, a source building might be a gravel/aggregate loading station, a concrete plant, a bus platform (for workers), etc. The construction office will then automatically send vehicles to take resources from source buildings and deliver them to construction sites.

Click on the "Purchase vehicle" [IMG editor/vehicle_buy_rub.png] button and purchase vehicles. The exact vehicles required will depend on the type of construction, but you will need buses, dump trucks, open-hull trucks, concrete mixers, and eventually cranes.

You can click on the "Assign construction" [IMG editor/tool_building_addconstruction.png] button to assign constructions, or if a construction office is idle, it will search and automatically help finish constructions.
19206: When will my constructions get built?
19207:
Clicking on any construction brings up the construction window.

Unless you're using Realistic mode, you can always choose to fund all or part of a construction with money by clicking on the "Fund construction" [IMG editor/buy_rub.png] [IMG editor/buy_dollar.png] button.

If the construction is already set to be funded, you can cancel this funding with the "Cancel contract" [IMG editor/btab_cancel_fundrub.png] button. This will stop spending money and construction will be ready to assign to any construction office.

If the construction is in progress and assigned to construction offices, you can force-stop construction with the "Stop construction" [IMG editor/btab_cancel_construction.png] button. This will remove the assignment from all construction offices and send all vehicles and workers away from the construction.

If the construction is stopped, you can assign the construction to any construction office to get it moving again, or you can click on "Start construction" [IMG editor/btab_start_construction.png] in the construction window. This will start construction, and if nearby construction offices are idle, they will automatically start work on it.
19208: What are the phases of construction?
19209:
There are many construction phases, like groundwork, steel framing, bricklaying, etc.

Every phase requires different resources and vehicles.

The most common requirement is workers [IMG editor/workers_workers_loedu.png]. All phases require manpower to finish. Eventually, instead of workers you can use vehicles. 

[IMA vehicles/service_caterpilar_big/preview.dds] [IMA vehicles/service_bulldozer_big/preview.dds] [IMA vehicles/service_paver/preview.dds] [IMA vehicles/service_mixer_t138/preview.dds] 

Excavator, asphalt paver, roller, etc. can completely replace manpower, so each construction phase could be completed without any workers present on the construction site!

[IMA vehicles/service_crane_kmz_5320/preview.dds]

Cranes do not replace workers. Cranes cannot complete construction without workers on the construction site, but they speed up construction, and some phases may require a crane to complete.

In the construction window (click on the construction), you can observe information about the current phase of construction, such as the resources required to complete, which vehicles are in use, and how many workers are present on the construction site.
19210: How do I use the railway construction office?
19211:
Click on [CATEGORY constindustry].

Select [TOOL rail_construction_office].

First, you should click on "Purchase vehicle" [IMG editor/train_buy_rub.png] and purchase a railway construction trainset, which is a special train for building railways.

You will also need workers. The maximum amount of workers is determined by the capacity of the rail construction trainset.

Unlike a regular construction office, the railway construction office does not need sources defined for resources, because you need to have all required resources for construction stored in the building. You can purchase what you require with "Purchase resources" [IMG editor/buy_rub.png].

After you have everything prepared, you can assign railway construction work to the railway construction office. If the railway construction office has any unengaged/free trainsets, they will automatically start work on the railway.
19212: How do I build things that don't have road connections?
19213:
Some constructions, such as playgrounds or statues, cannot be connected to a construction office by road.

These constructions need to be connected to roads via footpaths instead. [IMG editor/infrastructure_pedestrian.png] Footpaths can directly connect to roads, forming a pedestrian crossing.

Build a road close to the building, then place a footpath that connects that road to the new building. Now it can be assigned to a construction office.
19214: How do I build secondary infrastructure (conveyors, pipeline, etc.)?
19215:
Construction of secondary infrastructure like "Conveyors" [IMG editor/tool_conveyor.png], "Pipelines" [IMG editor/tool_pipe.png], "Factory Connections" [IMG editor/tool_factoryconnection.png], and "Power lines" [IMG editor/infrastructure_eletric_low.png] works the same as any other construction.

Even when there is no road connection between, for example, the conveyor and the construction office, there needs to be a connection to each start or end point. 

For example, if a conveyor is going to be built running from Factory A to Factory B, and the construction of the conveyor is assigned to a construction office, that office will need a road connection to Factory A and a road connection to Factory B.
19300: Can you tell me more about connecting infrastructure to buildings?
19301:
When placing a building (or certain other kinds of infrastructure), there are symbols on the building representing its connection points to roads, railways, footpaths, etc.:

[IMA editor/screenmarks/roadconnection2.png] [IMA editor/screenmarks/roadconnection3.png] One-way connection to road

[IMA editor/screenmarks/railconnection.png] Connection to railway

[IMA editor/screenmarks/railconnection2.png] [IMA editor/screenmarks/railconnection3.png] One-way connection to railway

[IMA editor/screenmarks/pedestrianconnection.png] Connection to footpath

[IMA editor/screenmarks/pipe_input.png] [IMA editor/screenmarks/pipe_output.png] Connection to pipeline (input/output)

[IMA editor/screenmarks/conveyor_input.png] [IMA editor/screenmarks/conveyor_output.png] Connection to conveyor (input/output)

[IMA editor/screenmarks/factoryconnection.png] Factory connection

[IMA editor/screenmarks/eletric_output.png] [IMG editor/screenmarks/eletric_output.png] Connection to powerlines 

[IMA editor/screenmarks/eletric_input2.png] [IMA editor/screenmarks/eletric_output2.png] Connection to powerlines (input/output) with option to set priority

When a connection is made, the symbol disappears, showing that this connection has been used and is no longer available for a new connection.
19302: How do I upgrade my roads?
19303:
You can upgrade roads at any time.

[IMA editor/tool_road_mud.png] > [IMA editor/tool_road_gravel.png] > [IMA editor/tool_road_asphalt.png] > [IMA editor/tool_road_asphaltside.png] 

For example, if you have a mud or gravel road, you can use the asphalt road tool and build a new road over the current one. Construction will begin and the original road will be changed to the newly chosen type.

Restriction (WIP): Currently, when upgrading roads, you can upgrade only one part of the road at a time. If the road you're upgrading contains crossings with other roads or footpaths, you will need to upgrade each part of the road network separately between crossings.
19304: How and why should I build footpaths?
19305:
Footpaths are very useful. Citizens can reach buildings by foot within a limited distance (approx. 300m). Roads are wide, and their curves cannot be very sharp, making them much less useful for short connections between citizens' destinations. 

With footpaths, you can make shortcuts between buildings. This allows citizens to reach more buildings by foot, and you don't need as dense a network of stores, platforms/stations, or other buildings to meet your citizens' needs.

Footpaths can connect to roads (pedestrian crossing) or directly to a building at a connection point. [IMG editor/screenmarks/pedestrianconnection.png]

To build a footpath:

Select [CATEGORY pedestrianway].

Select a type of footpath.

[TOOL pedestrianway_mud] [TOOL pedestrianway]

You are ready to construct a footpath just as you would build a road.
19306: How do I build railway tracks?
19307:
The basic mechanics of building rail tracks are similar to building roads. 

There are three types of railway track available:

[IMA editor/tool_rail_wood.png] [IMA editor/tool_rail_concrete.png] [IMA editor/tool_rail_eletric.png]

Note that electric locomotives and trams can only use electrified railways.

When laying out tracks, you can choose to build multi-track with the near-snap option. Toggle snapping to near railways to create multi-track railways to make new tracks automatically snap to nearby railways:

[IMG editor/ico_bottom_nearsnap.png] [IMG editor/checkbox_on.png] 

The near rail section beyond which you can build multi-track is highlighted in yellow.
19309:
Factory connections are special connections for use between two close buildings to automatically transport resources between those buildings.

Select [CATEGORY factorycons].

Select [TOOL factoryconnection].

You need to draw this special road between two buildings at their resource connection points.

[IMA editor/screenmarks/factoryconnection.png]

Buildings need to be close to each other for a factory connection to work.

Example of use:
You have built a factory. You want to increase its storage capacity, so you build a warehouse close to the factory. You can now connect the factory to the warehouse with a "Factory Connection." The factory will give resources to or take resources from this warehouse automatically, without the need to transport them with trucks or trains.

You can also use factory connections to load cargo to multiple buildings at once by placing a cargo loading station between them and connecting both factories to the loading station with a factory connection.

Note:
Only certain resources can be transported by this type of connection: namely, resources that can be stored in open-space storage (wood, boards, steel, etc.) or a warehouse (food, alcohol, meat, cement, etc.)
19311:
Pipelines are special connections between two buildings to transport liquid resources like oil, fuel, and bitumen.

Select [CATEGORY pipelines].

Use [TOOL pipe].

You need to draw this special connection between two buildings at their resource connection points. Note that the input and output connections are different:

Input - [IMA editor/screenmarks/pipe_input.png]

Output - [IMA editor/screenmarks/pipe_output.png]

Pipelines have a length restriction, but you can place one or more pumping engines between connection points to extend it:

[TOOL pipe_pumping_station]

[TOOL pipe_pumping_station]

You can chain these pumps together to carry resources over greater distances.

If you want to load liquid resources onto a train, you will need a special pumping station:

[TOOL rail_pumping_station]

You will need to connect the train station and source building(s) to this station with pipelines.

Road vehicles can load or unload liquids directly from their source building.
19313:
Conveyors are special connections between two buildings to transport aggregate materials such as gravel, iron, coal, etc.

Select [CATEGORY conveyors].

Use [TOOL conveyor].

You need to draw this special connection between two buildings at their resource connection points. Note that the input and output connections are different:

[IMA editor/screenmarks/conveyor_input.png] - Input

[IMA editor/screenmarks/conveyor_output.png] - Output

Conveyors have a length restriction, but you can extend it with one or more conveyor engines:

[TOOL conveyor_engine]

You can chain these engines together to carry aggregates over greater distances. Conveyor engines are also helpful if you need to make a detour to bend over another conveyor or make a sharp angle.

To load or unload aggregates onto a train, you need a special loading and unloading station. You will need to connect this special station with the source building by conveyor.

[TOOL rail_station_rumble_unloading] 

[TOOL rail_station_rumble_loading.png]

Road vehicles can load and unload directly from the source building, but loading of aggregate materials is much slower this way. You can speed it up by using special aggregate loading and unloading stations for road vehicles.

[TOOL road_cargo_rumble_unloading]

[TOOL road_cargo_rumble_loading]
19400: How can my republic become energy-independent and produce its own power?
19401:
Select "Constructions" [IMA editor/btab_start_construction.png] from the top panel.

Select "Power related" [IMA editor/building_eletric.png] category

Select a type of power plant:

[IMA editor/tool_powerplant_coal.png]

(WIP, only one power plant available currently)

A power plant is a special factory where resources (like coal) are transformed into electric energy.

Power plants automatically distribute energy to nearby buildings. You can click on "View electric connection" [IMG editor/btab_eletric.png] to check which buildings the power plant will supply.

[IMA editor/tool_eletric_low2.png] >> [IMA editor/tool_eletric_substation.png]

You can distribute power to distant buildings via power lines and substations. See additional topics for this.
19403:
Power is distributed in the following ways:

1) High-voltage power lines [IMA editor/infrastructure_eletric_high.png]

These have a high power throughput but can't interact with most buildings, so you will usually need to run these lines into a transformer. See the additional topic "Building high-voltage power lines" for a detailed description.

2) Medium-voltage power lines [IMA editor/infrastructure_eletric_low.png]

The power carried from high-voltage lines needs to be brought down before it can interact with most kinds of infrastructure. Connect the high-voltage line with a transformer, and you'll be able to use the transformer's medium-voltage connections to run medium-voltage wires into substations or some buildings. See the additional topic "Building medium-voltage power lines" for a detailed description.

3) Directly, by low-voltage underground wiring:

[IMA editor/tool_powerplant_coal.png] [IMA editor/tool_eletric_substation.png]

These power lines are invisible and built automatically around power plants or substations. Just build a substation wherever you want to distribute the power directly to buildings around it, using the yellow lines to see all the buildings that will be powered by it. You can also see those power connections when you mouse over the icon "View electric connections" in buildings.
19405:
Select "Infrastructure" [IMA editor/maintab_infrastructure.png] from the top panel.

Select the "High-voltage wires" [IMA editor/infrastructure_eletric_high.png] category.

Select a high-voltage wire:

[IMA editor/tool_eletric_high.png]

You can connect high-voltage wires to buildings at high-voltage connection points

[IMA editor/screenmarks/eletric_output.png]

High-voltage wires can go from power plants to transformers. You can then use the transformer's medium-voltage connection points to run medium-voltage wires to your substations.

[IMA editor/tool_powerplant_coal.png] >> [IMA editor/tool_eletric_high.png] >> [IMA editor/tool_eletric_transformator.png] >> [IMA editor/infrastructure_eletric_low.png] >> [IMA editor/tool_eletric_substation.png]
19407:
Select "Infrastructure" [IMA editor/maintab_infrastructure.png] from the top panel.

Select the "Medium-voltage wires" [IMA editor/infrastructure_eletric_low.png] category.

Select a medium-voltage wire:

[IMA editor/tool_eletric_low0.png] [IMA editor/tool_eletric_low1.png] [IMA editor/tool_eletric_low2.png]

You can connect medium-voltage wires to buildings at medium-voltage connection points:

[IMA editor/screenmarks/eletric_output.png]

Most power plants have some medium-voltage connection points, but you can use high-voltage wires to carry electricity farther before stepping the voltage down at a transformer. You can then use the transformer's medium-voltage connection points to run wires from the transformer into your substations.

[IMA editor/tool_powerplant_coal.png] >> [IMA editor/infrastructure_eletric_low.png] >> [IMA editor/tool_eletric_substation.png]

[IMA editor/tool_eletric_transformator.png] >> [IMA editor/infrastructure_eletric_low.png] >> [IMA editor/tool_eletric_substation.png]
19408: How does buying and selling power work?
19409:
Placed along Soviet or Western borders, there are special buildings, "Foreign Power Connections," where you can purchase or sell power.

[IMA editor/tool_eletric_transformator_customin.png]

Click on this building to open its window.

You can switch this building between two modes:

-Import (purchase) mode
You can set the maximum amount of energy you want to import from foreign sources. You will be charged in the nation's currency according to your power consumption. You can view the purchase price here as well.

-Export (sell) mode
You can set the maximum amount of energy you want to export to foreign countries. You will be paid in the nation's currency according to your power consumption, up to the maximum set. You can view the sell price in this window as well.
19500: How do I make sure my vehicles have fuel?
19501:
All road vehicles need access to a gas station.

Select [CATEGORY roads].

Select [TOOL gas_station_v2].

If you are transporting goods or resources long distances, it is best to have gas stations near both start and end locations!

If a vehicle is out of fuel and can't find a gas station, an icon [IMG editor/vehiclewarning_fuel.png] is displayed over the vehicle, and the vehicle stops. If the vehicle finds a gas station, it will automatically go there to refuel. You can see the fuel status in the vehicle window (click on the vehicle).

Fuel needs to be stored at the gas station. You can deliver fuel with cistern trucks or purchase it directly with the [IMG editor/buy_rub.png] icon.

Don't forget, electricity is needed for pumping fuel!
19502: How does fuel distribution work for trains?
19503:
Select [CATEGORY railways].

Select [TOOL rail_gas_station].

If you are transporting goods or resources long distances, it is best to have a refueling station near the start and end locations. It is recommended that a fuel station be placed along your trains' routes to ensure they don't run out of fuel. As a train goes through, it will refuel if under 35%% fuel capacity.

If a train is out of fuel and can't find a refueling station, an icon [IMG editor/vehiclewarning_fuel.png] is displayed over the train, and the train stops. If the train finds a refueling station, it will automatically go there to refuel. You can see the fuel status in the vehicle window (click on the train).

Fuel needs to be stored at a rail refueling station. Fuel can be delivered to this station via cistern train, cistern truck, or direct pipeline, or you can purchase it directly by clicking on the [IMG editor/buy_rub.png] icon.

Don't forget, electricity is needed for pumping fuel!
19504: How do I connect an electrified railway to the power network?
19505:
Select [CATEGORY railways].

Select [TOOL rail_trafo].

Construct the building, then connect it to your railway network using the electrified tracks.

[IMA editor/infrastructure_eletric_low.png] >> [IMA editor/tool_rail_trafo.png] >> [IMA editor/tool_rail_eletric.png]

Electricity will flow from this connection through the electrified tracks in your network. If an electrified track is not connected to a railroad electric connection, an icon [IMG editor/rail_eletric.png] will be displayed over the track. 

Electric locomotives or trams can only utilize electrified railway.

If there is no voltage on the railway, an icon [IMG editor/vehiclewarning_eletric.png] will be displayed over the train without power.
19507:
Giving citizens access to their own cars has some benefits besides just increasing the range of the buildings they can access. First, having a car will increase citizens' loyalty. Second, it can ensure that educated workers can easily reach the destinations where their expertise is needed, so those workplaces can always be staffed with experts.

Car access is managed through parking lots - [TOOL parking_small]

Parking lots can be built near residential areas and workplaces or areas where citizens spend their free time. If a citizen has a car but no appropriate workplace is available within walking distance, they will search for another workplace that they can reach in their car. The same applies to their free time activities; if there are no shops or activities near their home, they will try to find them near parking lots they can drive to.

When you open the window of any parking lot, you can see which parking lots are reachable from the selected parking lot:

[IMA editor/btab_cars.png] - [LANGSTR 331]

There are two options for distributing cars to citizens:

1) You can purchase (or bring in brand-new) personal cars directly at parking lots. Each parking lot has settings, and personal cars can be assigned according to age, education, and government loyalty level.

2) You can also distribute personal cars through a car dealership building - [TOOL cardealer]. In this building, brand-new personal cars are brought in and then distributed to citizens.
19509:
Airplanes are a very fast but expensive form of transportation.

To operate airplanes, first you need to build a runway.

Select [CATEGORY airplanes].

Then select [TOOL create_airroad_fly].

Next, build an airplane parking area. This is similar to a depot for road vehicles or trains, and you can purchase airplanes here.

[TOOL airplaneparking_30]

After that, connect the airplane parking area to the runways using taxiways.

[TOOL create_airroad]

You can also build terminals and connect them to the runways.

[TOOL airport_terminal]

[TOOL airport_terminal_cargo2]

Don't forget that to operate an airplane, you'll need to have a built and staffed control tower near the airport.

Also, don't forget that bigger airplanes need longer runways. This information is described in the airplane's vehicle properties.

[TOOL control_tower]

Aside from the standard vehicle errors, airplanes have some unique error icons that might show up:

[IMG editor/vehiclewarning_controltower.png] An airplane cannot land or take off because there are not enough workers in the control tower.

[IMG editor/vehiclewarning_airplanefull.png] An airplane cannot land or take off because runways or taxiways are occupied by other airplanes, so it needs to wait.

You can send airplanes beyond the borders to Soviet or Western countries. To do this, you need to click on the special icon to add this stop to the airplane's schedule.

[IMG editor/export_rub.png] - [LANGSTR 6421]

[IMG editor/export_dollar.png] - [LANGSTR 6420]

If you have a brand-new airplane, clicking on this icon and then launching the airplane will result in the airplane being sold as a brand-new one to Western or Soviet countries.

There are no specific refueling stations for airplanes; airplanes are simply refueled in terminals.
19511:
Ships are a large-capacity but slow means of transporting passengers or cargo.

To operate a ship, you just need to build a dock, which works similar to a depot for road vehicles or trains.

[TOOL ship_dock_small]

You can purchase a new ship there.

Then, you can build your passenger or cargo harbors.

[TOOL harbor_passanger_small]

[TOOL harbor_cargo_small]

Keep in mind that bigger ships cannot fit in small harbors. Information about the maximum ship length is described in the strip when selecting the harbor on the dock from the build menu.

You can use the buoy tool to place buoys, which will be especially useful if your sea routes are busy and you want to avoid collisions between ships.

[TOOL bojka_red]

You can send ships beyond the borders to Soviet or Western countries. To do this, you need to click on the special icon to add this stop to the ship's schedule.

[IMA editor/export_rub.png] - [LANGSTR 6421]

[IMA editor/export_dollar.png] - [LANGSTR 6420]

If you have a brand-new ship, clicking on this icon and then launching the ship will result in the ship being sold as a brand-new one to Western or Soviet countries.

There are no specific refueling stations for ships; ships are refueled in harbors.
19513:
You can manufacture your own vehicles. Manufacturing vehicles works similarly to any other factories. You bring in input resources and workers, and the vehicle will be manufactured.

Build the appropriate production lines to manufacture different kinds of vehicles:

[TOOL production_vehicle] to manufacture road vehicles, forklifts, or cableway cabins.

[TOOL production_train2] to manufacture trains.

[TOOL drydock] to manufacture ships.

[TOOL production_airplane] to manufacture aircraft.

However, you need to purchase a blueprint for the vehicle before you can start manufacturing it.

To purchase a blueprint, open the window of the production line and click on one of these two buttons:

[IMG editor/blueprint_rub.png] - [LANGSTR 2029]

[IMG editor/blueprint_usd.png] - [LANGSTR 2030]

After purchasing the blueprint, you need to set it up for manufacturing:

[IMG editor/blueprint_set.png] - [LANGSTR 2025]

>>Newly produced road vehicles:

•You can send a newly produced road vehicle to a workplace by using the button in the vehicle window.

•You can send a flatbed truck to load the vehicle and unload it into a vehicle storage or a new workplace.

•You can send a flatbed truck with the newly produced vehicle to be unloaded at a customs house. By transporting the vehicle this way, it will be sold as brand-new.

>>Newly produced trains:

•You can send brand-new locomotives to rail depots.

•For wagons and locomotives, you can use another locomotive and order it to load the brand-new trains at the production line and bring them to the railway depot, vehicle storage, or workplace.

•You can order this locomotive to unload those joined trains at a customs house and sell them as brand-new.

>>Newly produced ships:

•After a ship is produced, you can set up a schedule for it like any other vehicle.

•You can send the ship beyond the borders to Soviet or Western countries. To do this, you need to click on the special icon to add this stop to the ship's schedule.

[IMG editor/export_rub.png] - [LANGSTR 6421]

[IMG editor/export_dollar.png] - [LANGSTR 6420]

>>Newly produced aircraft:

•Don't forget to attach the airplane parking area to the airplane production line to be able to store your new aircraft.

•After an aircraft is produced, you can set up a schedule for it like other vehicles.

You can send aircraft beyond the borders to Soviet or Western countries. To do this, you need to click on the special icon to add this stop to the aircraft's schedule.

[IMG editor/export_rub.png] - [LANGSTR 6421]

[IMG editor/export_dollar.png] - [LANGSTR 6420]

If you have a brand new aircraft, clicking on this icon and then launching the airplane will result in the aircraft being sold as a brand-new one to Western or Soviet countries.

Notes:

*Launching the vehicle via the schedule menu will mark the vehicle as used, and it can only be sold as a used vehicle.
**Bringing the brand-new vehicle to any of the workplaces will mark the vehicle as used, and it can only be sold as a used vehicle.
19514: How do I build an airport?
19515:
You can construct airport taxiways and runways with the construction office. To do this, you will need to build a gate for airplanes that will allow construction vehicles to access the runways.

[TOOL airport_road_connection]
19517:
To place a signal, open the railway category. When placing signals, you will split the rail track into blocks. You can see these blocks turn different colors when placing the signal.

A single click will place a two-way signal. When you click with the signal tool again on the same place, you will get a one-way signal (click again to reverse its direction).

Important: Trains are allowed to pass a one-way signal only in one direction!!

There are two types of signals in the game:

[TOOL rail_semaphore] - The signal is red when the subsequent block is occupied by other trains.

[TOOL rail_semaphore_chain] - The signal is red only when all exits from the blocks are not free. The signal is blue when at least one exit from the block is free. Here, it depends on where exactly the train will go; it might stop on a blue signal if the train's intended route is not free.

Please find additional guides on the Steam Workshop or the internet about this topic. It is a very complicated topic. 
Moreover, note that the game implements path signal mechanics, so sometimes it is okay for a train to enter the block even on the red signal color when there is no collision with the train in the block. 

Additionally, sometimes a train may not be allowed to enter the block even on the green color to prevent a deadlock (probably because the other train is about to enter the block or rail track).

There are additional tools for signal placement:

[TOOL rail_semaphorecancel] - To remove a signal.

[TOOL rail_semaphore_double] - To place two signals on a double track.

[TOOL rail_semaphore_mixedchain] - To place a mixed signal (from one side chain, from the other side block signal).

[TOOL rail_semaphore_waypoint] - Aside from signals, you can place waypoints on the track. 

Note that both signals and waypoints can be used as waypoints in a train's schedule. This is useful when you want to force a train to go through a specific track.
19518: How do I use technical service buildings?
19519:
Open the 

[CATEGORY forcitizens] 

or 

[CATEGORY roads] menu 

and click on [TOOL technical_services] to build a technical service building.

A technical service station can serve three different tasks:

1)Handling garbage
Purchase garbage trucks and set the destination for each type of garbage, and the trucks will carry out the garbage from the buildings and bins and move it to the set destination. There are two sizes of garbage bins (small and large) that a building might use, so you will need to match your garbage collection vehicles with the garbage bin size in the technical office's operating range.

Only garbage from storages marked with the special icon [IMG editor/demand_container.png] will be handled; if a factory produces waste as an output (i.e., waste-processing buildings), it will be treated as a regular resource and must be handled via lines or a distribution office. 

2) Handling drinking water and sewage
You can purchase trucks to move water or sewage. Set the source building for drinking water and the destination for sewage, and the vehicles will deliver water to buildings where it is not available by pipeline or collect sewage and bring it to a discharge site. You can also use unconnected substations, and water trucks will then bring water to the substation, which will then automatically supply the buildings nearby. 19520: What is a garbage container transfer?
19521:
Garbage container transfers are a special kind of storage that can hold garbage and serve as a central collection point for an area. Garbage is loaded and unloaded much faster at these sites since all the garbage is already placed and sorted into large bins that can be loaded onto vehicles.

To build a garbage transfer, open the [CATEGORY waste] 

menu and select one of the container transfer storages.

Click on the [TOOL containerstorage_small].

Technical services can be told to bring all or certain types of garbage to these storages, and the garbage can then be further moved along the waste processing chain with the efficiency of quick unloading and centralized location.
19523:
Open the [CATEGORY waste] menu 

and select one of the container stands:

[TOOL containerstand_small]

[TOOL bigcontainerstand]

Almost every building in the game produces garbage, and each building has its own default storage/container for waste. However, with many buildings in residential areas, garbage trucks from technical services will need to visit every building. Also, many buildings in residential areas may not be connected via roads, only via footpaths.

To solve this issue, you can build container stands, which will act as a central location for garbage collection. When you build a container stand near buildings, the buildings will use the stands as the default destination for their waste collection instead of their small internal garbage storage.

By hovering over the icon 

[IMG editor/btab_waste.png] [LANGSTR 47512]

you can see if a building is in range of a container stand, or if a container stand is in range of a building.

Container stands can also be used for industrial buildings. For those industrial buildings that are not directly working with garbage as input or output resources (i.e., waste-processing buildings), you can extend the internal garbage storage via a factory connection to a dump or garbage transfer.

Additionally, you can assign different areas of the container stand to be used for different kinds of garbage, so that waste can remain separated.
19524: How do I maintain my vehicles?
19525:
Open [CATEGORY roads].

Click on [TOOL garage_small].

Repair stations are buildings that perform vehicle repairs. These buildings require workers and replacement parts to operate.

When placing a repair station, it will have an orange range displayed. Specific buildings will be highlighted in orange, representing a connection to the repair stations. For example, if you are placing a repair station near a railway depot, the depot will turn orange. When the repair station is placed, it will be connected to the train depot, allowing the repair station to repair trains that are inside the depot.

Repair stations can also have covered trucks that operate over long distances, visiting various workplaces to fix vehicles.

If you open the repair station's window, you'll see connected buildings highlighted in orange. You can also see the station's roaming range indicated by a yellow highlight, as well as any buildings in that range highlighted in yellow. Areas and buildings in this range can be reached by the station's open-hull trucks for mobile repair.

1) [IMA editor/lines_vehicles.png] Road Vehicles 

Road vehicles assigned to standard transit lines, such as buses, can simply visit repair stations since they are connected to the road network. To avoid interruption, you could also build an end station that is in range of the repair station, and put that end station on the vehicle's line. Repairs will take place while the vehicle waits in the end station.

Road vehicles assigned to workplaces, such as construction or distribution offices, will be repaired at their respective workplaces via the mobile repair trucks. To make this work, you will need to have covered trucks set to work in the repair station. These trucks will then visit the workplaces of the vehicles in need of repairs and fix them. Another option is to have such workplaces built close to the repair stations (within the orange highlighted range).

2) [IMA editor/tool_trolleybus_depo.png] [IMA editor/tool_tram_depo_small.png] Trams & Trolleybuses

To repair trams or trolleybuses, you need to have a depot or an end station in range of the repair station (within the orange highlight). Trams and trolleybuses will visit the depot when they need repairs, or repairs will take place while they wait in the end station.

3) [IMA editor/lines_trains.png] Trains

To repair trains, you need to have a depot or an end station in range of the repair station (within the orange highlight). Trains will visit the depot when they need repairs, or repairs will take place while they wait in the end station.

Trains assigned to workplaces, such as track builders in rail construction offices, can be repaired by covered trucks from the repair station, or you can build a repair station in range of the rail construction office.

4) [IMA editor/lines_ships.png] Ships

You will need to build a repair station in range of a dock or harbor to repair ships.
Important note: If you have a repair station near a dock, a ship assigned to a line will not automatically visit that dock (similar to trains).

5) [IMA editor/lines_airplanes.png] Airplanes & Helicopters

You will need to build a repair station near airplane parking areas or terminals to repair airplanes and helicopters.
Important note: If you have a repair station near an airplane parking area, airplanes assigned to a line will not automatically visit that parking area. However, helicopters on lines will automatically visit a parking area or heliport that is connected to a repair station.

Helicopters assigned to workplaces can also be repaired by covered trucks sent from repair stations.

6) No maintenance required:

Cableway cars, train wagons, and cargo containers do not require maintenance.
19526: How do resources move throughout a network?
19527:
Warehouses and other kinds of storage are passive buildings: they cannot push or pull (take) resources. For aggregates and liquids, you can place conveyor engines or liquid-pumping stations in between storages (or other buildings) to move resources from Building A to Building B. For more complex factory networks, forklift garages are required to move resources between factory connections.

So, this setup will NOT WORK:

Factory A [IMG editor/tool_factoryconnection.png] Storage A [IMG editor/tool_factoryconnection.png] Storage B [IMG editor/tool_factoryconnection.png] Factory B

(Factory A will push resources to Storage A, but it will not push them further to Storage B. Factory B can take resources from Storage B, but it will be empty). The same applies to conveyors or pipelines without engines in between buildings.

This setup will work:

Factory A [IMG editor/tool_factoryconnection.png] Storage A [IMG editor/tool_factoryconnection.png] Factory B

(Factory A will push resources to Storage A, Factory B can take resources from Storage A).

If a vehicle comes to a station or building, it can move resources to and from buildings that are connected to it.

Factory A [IMG editor/tool_factoryconnection.png] Cargo Station A [IMG editor/tool_factoryconnection.png] Factory B [IMG editor/tool_factoryconnection.png] Factory C

When a vehicle comes to load/unload resources at Cargo Station A, it can also load/unload resources from/to Factory A or Factory B, but not from/to Factory C.

[TOOL forklift_crossing]

With factory connection crossings, you can create a complex network and connect multiple factories, even if they are farther apart. However, to actually move resources around this network, you will need to use forklift garages:

[TOOL forklift_station]

You will need to purchase forklifts and assign them buildings, specifying what to load and unload from each building. Forklifts will then handle the job automatically, but the resources will move much slower than a direct factory connection.

Refueling & construction of the complex network of factory connections using construction offices:

As forklift garages/stations are connected to the road network, this connection is used for construction vehicles and refueling vehicles. Forklifts can be refueled in their garages.
19531:
Open [CATEGORY factorycons].

Choose one of the distribution offices:

[TOOL distribution_office_small]

Distribution offices are a powerful tool that allows you to specify source and destination buildings for all kinds of resources. Trucks are then sent to transport goods only when needed, saving fuel and limiting traffic. 

In the distribution office task manager, each building can be given a threshold for vehicles to deliver or collect resources to or from that building, so your factories don't run out of inputs their outputs are sent to their next destination. You can use this building to sell and buy goods; since the customs house doesn't have a threshold, it will only be visited when another building's threshold is met and there is no higher priority task.

Example: Your clothing factory is set to load (collect) at 50%%, and its storage is 70%% full. Your warehouse for citizen use is set to unload (deliver) clothing at 30%%, and its storage is also 70%% full. A truck will load from the factory and unload at the assigned customs house, since the load threshold is met and the goods aren't needed elsewhere.)

Important note:

The distribution office CANNOT be used for:
a) distributing brand-new vehicles
b) transporting resources packed in containers
c) moving the containers themselves.

55552:
We continue our journey to transform Kamchatka into the backbone of Soviet production.

In this objective, we will introduce railway manufacturing.

This will help expand our train lines, but most importantly, we will be able to export trains to meet new Soviet demands.

I am thrilled by how Kamchatka is able to push boundaries in advancing production engineering.
55553:
Our colleagues have designed a robust locomotive production line that will stand out among the competition.

Now let's begin the construction of the railway production line!

As always, I recommend utilizing our construction offices. It will minimize excessive spending on outsourced labor and resource transportation costs.

The magnificence of the production line factory we've built is truly breathtaking.

Comrade, this is just the beginning.

Set up transportation infrastructure for resources and workers to initiate production.

Ensure your railway network is connected to the factory, which will enable the export of locomotives via rail.

However, they're impatient and eager to see the first delivery of locomotives without delay.

They are offering a bonus of 100,000 rubles if we export all 5 locomotives within the next 60 days.

To proceed, arrange a dedicated line on another locomotive to load it from the plant and unload it at the customs house.

Alternatively, you can construct a ship dock, dispatch the locomotives and wagons there, and load them onto a cargo ship to be unloaded at the border.

The Soviets are celebrating our early delivery, and as promised, they will grant us a bonus of 100,000 rubles.

Our new factory shines as a beacon, guiding Kamchatka toward advanced engineering.

Our future lies in helicopter manufacturing, which will enable us not only to meet Soviet demands but also to expand our construction capabilities.

To make this happen, we will construct the aircraft production line.

Our colleagues have designed a production line factory that can produce both airplanes and helicopters.

For its construction, I recommend utilizing our construction offices.

This will help to minimize excessive spending on outsourced labor and resource transportation costs.

Select Build Heliport, and see the green dots located on one side of the factory.

Construct 3 heliports for now. The newly produced helicopters will appear there.

This is a huge achievement that will boost not just exports but our whole country's transportation.

Now, let us concentrate on establishing the transport of resources and workers.

Thanks to our excellent cooperation, they will provide us with the blueprint.

However, they need the initial delivery of 5 helicopters on time, within the next 90 days.

If we accomplish this, the Soviets will grant us a bonus of 100,000 rubles.
55583:
Comrade, this is an incredible success!

Everyone is celebrating the newly produced helicopters. And for meeting the deadline, we'll be granted a bonus of 100,000 rubles.

The new production line factory in Kamchatka marks yet another advanced engineering marvel. The entire Soviet Union is talking about our achievements, and rightfully so.

We're ahead of all competitors like never before.

We're ahead of all competitors like never before.
55591: Continue Kamchatka's evolution into a powerhouse of Soviet production. Next will be ship manufacturing, which massively expands the nation's exports and strengthens the country's infrastructure.
55592:
We will finalize our endeavor to transform Kamchatka into the Soviet's core production hub. Our land logistics have greatly assisted their landlocked regions, but our production capacity is now great enough for us to become a part of their robust naval logistics network.

As this region rapidly grows, we anticipate the scale of both our production and consumption will increase dramatically, requiring vast amounts of resoures to be both exported and imported for daily life.

Ships will play a pivotal role. They can move resources on a massive scale that is not possible with traditional road or railway networks.

Let's be ready for the future and ensure Kamchatka will be the most essential Soviet ally!
55593:
I'm thrilled to announce a advancement in production engineering, unprecedented in Kamchatka and the entire region.

We will build a massive drydock, a production factory situated on the coast, dedicated to manufacturing the largest ships ever witnessed in our region.

I suggest you order our construction offices to manage this whole construction.
55595:
Wow, the new coastal industry area looks absolutely breathtaking.

This concludes our transformation into an engineering production powerhouse for the Soviets, positioning us ahead of all other regions.

Comrade, my work here is done; our industry now stands as planned. Make sure we utilize all our factories to the maximum, and the victory will be ours.

If we achieve that, we'll receive another bonus of 100,000 rubles.
